name: BERRY, Carol

headline.note: Two dated public-sector spells and six dated nonprofit spells are documented, but no source establishes substantive full-time status. Nonprofit, party, political-staff and elected-office spells are excluded from both headline sectors. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.employer: Family Planning Australia (historical legal/employer name not verified)
career_spells.evidence_note: First speech calls this one of her first jobs and describes reproductive-rights campaign work. Dates, hours and the employer's then-current legal name remain unresolved. Follow-up2026-10-02: public professional-profile search index explicitly associates Family Planning Australia with January2004–December2005. Month precision retained; overlaps with Greens office, Organ adviser observation and December2005 PIAC commencement are unresolved, not added as separate full-time duration. Historical legal name, hours and breaks still unknown.

open_questions: Can primary employer records confirm the profile January2004–December2005 Family Planning dates, historical legal employer, exact transitions, hours and breaks?
What were the appointment/payroll dates, pay status, hours and leave for the Greens national-secretary and Michael Organ adviser roles?
Were the dated PIAC, CID, IWHC, NSW Ombudsman, NDIA and Disability Trust spells substantively full-time, and were there material leave or breaks?
Do primary employer or government personnel records refine the month-only transitions and explain the 3–5 May 2025 Trust/House overlap?
What are the exact dates and paid/unpaid status of2025 campaign leave from The Disability Trust?
Can the Greens honour-roll presumed end be confirmed, and CRC governance and representative roles be dated?
research_notes: Systematic follow-up2026-10-01. Repaired missing required research_notes field; preserved every existing supported spell/source and the separate open_questions. Baseline records supplied month-level paid-work dates and unknown hours; none have been promoted to full-time from title or salary.

Primary PIAC annual reports now support both2005–2008 employment endpoints, specific role and external governance/advocacy work. Greens honour roll supplies2003–2005 office dates with explicit presumed-end qualification. Trust employer departure notice reread and confirmed5May2025; pre-election interview establishes campaign leave but not its dates/pay.

Public sources searched for Family Planning dates/legal name, NDIA/Ombudsman hours, professional profiles, historical annual reports, maternity/campaign leave, party office and Royal Commission evidence. Unrelated US realtor, clinician, academic and charity-manager results excluded. Generic full-time staff figures and other employees’ maternity annotations are not evidence about Berry.

Government hearing15February2023 corroborates CEO entry. Exhibit32-92 (TDT.9999.0001.0001) is a remaining document lead; detailed statement not retrieved in this pass. Further priorities: personal hours/leave for public-sector spells; Family Planning and Organ adviser boundaries; Greens remuneration; exact campaign leave; CRC governance dates. Last follow-up2026-10-01; advance across all batches before revisiting exhausted broad queries.

Second follow-up2026-10-02 materially dates Family Planning work from the public professional-profile index; primary confirmation and simultaneous-role allocation remain open. Royal Commission exhibit32-092 lead retrieved: organisational evidence, not personal hours. May2025 successor recruitment pack identifies a replacement process but is not evidence of Berry contract hours. Broad exact-name searches produce US namesakes, excluded.

Next targeted leads: historical2004–05 Family Planning personnel/annual reports, Michael Organ office records and contemporaneous pay/hours evidence for Ombudsman/NDIA. Do not repeat generic biographies or interpret general staff policies as Berry employment status.

Further2October pass: PIAC2008 staff appendix already captured, no new personal-hours evidence. Green magazine Issue13 p11 clarifies adjacent full-time campaign wording describes John, not Berry. Organ office notice titled New MP's office up and running (ParlInfo media/pressrel/EJW86) publicly indexes Berry as lawyer/former Cunningham candidate, but full text returned (403) Forbidden and indexed context did not establish exact employment commencement. Retain as lead without converting notice date into start. Southern Highlands Express19February2025 retrospectively reports advising Organ during2002 election, which does not distinguish campaign advice from paid parliamentary employment. Historical Family Planning legal identity and public-service hours remain open; no substantive fact newly resolved in this pass.
